prompt.context: Your client is a dominant auto manufacturer in the US. You have been hired to implement a cost reduction program.
prompt.question: Where would you start and what are your recommendations?

framework: Stage 1 – Problem Identification: Break down cost structure into fixed costs (overheads, plants, capital equipment) and variable costs (labor, direct material costs); benchmark against competitors
Stage 2 – Recommend Solution: Address the root cause of excess component variants by standardizing and modularizing components across models to restore supplier economies of scale
Stage 3 – Implement the Solution: Develop a stakeholder engagement plan covering manufacturing engineers, designers, sales & marketing, and finance to gain buy-in

questions.prompt: What are the main cost components for an auto manufacturer, and which area is underperforming vs. competitors?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure costs into fixed (overheads, plants, capital equipment) and variable (labor, direct material costs). Benchmarking reveals that Direct Material Costs are significantly higher than competitors. Root cause: too many component variants per model. Example: one family sedan has 24 variants of steering wheels, preventing supplier economies of scale. Client has 30+ chassis platforms vs. competitor's 12.

questions.prompt: How would you reduce the excess component variants? Walk through the steering wheel example.
questions.guidance: Step 1 – Apply similarity criteria (design, parameters, requirements, overlapping parts) to consolidate variants. This reduces steering wheel variants from 24 to 10. Step 2 – Decompose each component into sub-parts by value: for a steering wheel the ring and frame are high-value base parts; covering and electronics are low-value customizations. Treat ring+frame as a standardized base (single variant for the supplier) and add coverings/electronics as customizations. This gives the supplier full economies of scale on the expensive base while preserving product differentiation.

questions.prompt: How would you implement this solution across the organization? Which stakeholders must you convince and what are their concerns?
questions.guidance: Manufacturing Engineers: process changes, retooling, integration of modular assembly. Designers: constraints on design freedom; reassurance that customization layer preserves brand differentiation. Sales & Marketing: concern that fewer variants reduce consumer choice; show that visible customization (coverings, electronics) is preserved. Finance: quantify cost savings from reduced SKUs, improved supplier pricing, and lower inventory.

brainstorming.prompt: What other areas beyond direct material costs could be explored in a broader cost reduction program for an auto manufacturer?

categories.name: Fixed Costs
ideas: Reduce capital equipment redundancy across platforms
Shared R&D spending across shared platforms

categories.name: Supply Chain
ideas: Long-term contracts to lock in pricing on commodities

categories.name: Product Portfolio
ideas: Eliminate low-volume models that require unique platforms
Accelerate platform sharing across brand segments
Reduce time-to-market by reusing certified components

recommendation: Immediately launch a component standardization initiative starting with the highest-cost, highest-variant parts (e.g., steering wheels, chassis platforms): reduce steering wheel variants from 24 to 10 using design-similarity criteria, then further to a modular base+customization architecture
Reduce chassis platforms from 30+ to a target closer to the competitor benchmark of 12, enabling significant economies of scale throughout the supply chain
risks: Designer and marketing resistance to perceived reduction in product differentiation
Supplier renegotiation complexity and potential transition costs
Risk of quality issues during the transition to new standardized components
next_steps: Conduct a full component audit to identify all high-variant, high-cost parts across the model range
Prioritize platform consolidation roadmap with engineering and product teams
Model financial savings from reduced SKUs and negotiate improved pricing with key suppliers
Run a pilot on one model line before rolling out program-wide
